# Cortex

> Cortex is an open-source (MIT) MCP server and studio for training robot policies with an AI agent, built on LeRobot, MuJoCo, ACT (Action Chunking Transformer) and the SO-101 (SO-ARM101) arm. Your coding agent describes the robot arm and the task over the Model Context Protocol; Cortex builds a MuJoCo simulation, collects simulator-verified demonstrations, trains an ACT or SmolVLA policy and evaluates it, with a human approving every step that costs money or moves hardware.

Cortex runs locally. MCP server (streamable HTTP): http://localhost:3000/mcp, tools named `cortex.<name>`. REST mirror: `GET http://localhost:8000/api/tools` lists every tool with its JSON schema; `POST http://localhost:8000/api/tools/<name>` calls one with the arguments as the JSON body. Studio (where people approve training): http://localhost:5173/studio.

Rules for agents: use ids from tool results, never invent them; agents never send motor commands (Cortex validates targets and executes with IK); training starts only after a human approves it in the studio; report only what the simulator measured.

**Connect** (pick your client):

Claude Code:

```sh
claude mcp add --transport http cortex http://localhost:3000/mcp
```

Cursor (`.cursor/mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cortex": {
      "url": "http://localhost:3000/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

VS Code (`.vscode/mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "servers": {
    "cortex": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://localhost:3000/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Any client (`.mcp.json`):

```json
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "cortex": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "http://localhost:3000/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

REST:

```sh
# every tool, with its JSON schema
curl http://localhost:8000/api/tools

# call one
curl -X POST http://localhost:8000/api/tools/get_project_state \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"project_id": "prj_…"}'
```

**Worked session** (MCP tool calls, ids abbreviated):

1. `cortex.start_intake` `{"prompt":"pick up the small water bottle and put it on the mat"}`: prj_… and typed questions, each with a ready patch.
2. `cortex.update_intake` `{"project_id":"prj_…","patch":{"zones":[{"name":"mat","center":[0.25,-0.1]}],"task":{"pick":"small_water_bottle","place":["mat"]}}}`: merged spec, what changed, questions left.
3. `cortex.build_simulation` `{"project_id":"prj_…"}`: MuJoCo scene and feasibility: jaw, torque, reach.
4. `cortex.capture_frame` `{"project_id":"prj_…","camera":"front"}`: a render to check against the real setup.
5. `cortex.start_agent_collection` `{"project_id":"prj_…","num_demos":12}`: ac_… and a job; only verified successes become episodes.
   Or drive the arm yourself: cortex.robot_start_episode, then robot_observe, robot_move, robot_gripper … robot_finish_episode.
6. `cortex.create_dataset_version` `{"project_id":"prj_…","wait_s":45}`: ds_…, a LeRobot v3 dataset with lineage.
7. `cortex.propose_training_job` `{"project_id":"prj_…","dataset_version_id":"ds_…","policy_type":"act"}`: tj_… with a GPU estimate; once a person approves it in the studio, cortex.launch_training_job runs it.
8. `cortex.evaluate_learned_policy` `{"project_id":"prj_…","checkpoint_id":"ck_…"}`: per-condition success with 95% intervals.
9. `cortex.improve_policy` `{"project_id":"prj_…","max_new_demos":5}`: weakest condition, targeted demos, a retraining proposal.

**Recipes by task** (MCP tools in order):

- Train a pick-and-place policy (SO-101, MuJoCo, ACT): `cortex.start_intake` → `cortex.update_intake` → `cortex.get_intake_status` → `cortex.build_simulation` → `cortex.capture_frame` → `cortex.start_agent_collection` → `cortex.get_collection_progress` → `cortex.create_dataset_version` → `cortex.propose_training_job` → `cortex.launch_training_job` → `cortex.get_project_state`. Answer intake questions with the patch each one carries until complete. Only simulator-verified successes become LeRobotDataset v3 episodes. Stop after propose_training_job and ask the person to approve it in the studio; never invent an approval token. A checkpoint (ck_...) appears in get_project_state when training ends.
- Collect demonstrations by driving the arm yourself: `cortex.robot_start_episode` → `cortex.robot_observe` → `cortex.robot_propose_grasp` → `cortex.robot_gripper` → `cortex.robot_move` → `cortex.robot_verify_grasp` → `cortex.robot_place` → `cortex.robot_check_success` → `cortex.robot_finish_episode`. You point at objects in the overhead image; Cortex validates workspace, reach, joint limits and collisions and executes with IK. The simulator, not you, decides success.
- Train from existing LeRobot data: `cortex.create_project` → `cortex.import_demonstrations` → `cortex.get_job` → `cortex.create_dataset_version` → `cortex.propose_training_job`. Imports episodes from a Hugging Face Hub dataset; they stay separate from simulation demos.
- Evaluate a policy in simulation: `cortex.evaluate_learned_policy` → `cortex.get_job` → `cortex.get_project_state` → `cortex.compare_experiments`. Three seeded MuJoCo branches (baseline, shifted object, dim lighting) on held-out seeds; success rates with 95% Wilson intervals; compare_experiments gives deltas and p-values.
- Improve a policy: `cortex.improve_policy` → `cortex.get_job` → `cortex.launch_training_job` → `cortex.evaluate_learned_policy`. Targets the weakest measured condition with new demonstrations in fresh seeds, then proposes retraining (needs approval). Also useful: cortex.analyze_dataset, cortex.get_failure_clusters (VLM clusters are hypotheses), cortex.recommend_demonstrations, cortex.get_next_actions.
- One-call start: `cortex.create_policy_project` → `cortex.get_collection_progress` → `cortex.train_from_agent_demonstrations`. Creates the project and starts autonomous agent collection in one call, then builds the dataset and proposes ACT training.

**Questions agents ask:**

- What is Cortex? Cortex is an open-source (MIT) MCP server that lets any AI agent train a physical robot with no human in the training loop. The agent describes the arm and a custom environment; Cortex builds it in MuJoCo, the agent collects its own demonstrations, trains an ACT policy, evaluates it and fixes its weak spots, then the policy moves to the physical arm. Built on LeRobot, MuJoCo, ACT and the SO-101 (SO-ARM101) arm.
- Why is Cortex built for agents? Agents can write and run software, but training a robot still needs people: someone to teleoperate demonstrations, label data, launch runs and judge results. Cortex turns each of those steps into an MCP tool with measured results, so an agent can run the whole loop itself. People only approve GPU spend and anything that moves hardware.
- How do I train a robot policy with an AI agent? Connect your agent to the Cortex MCP server, then ask for the task in plain words. The agent calls cortex.start_intake and cortex.update_intake to describe the arm, objects and goal, cortex.build_simulation for the MuJoCo scene, cortex.start_agent_collection for demonstrations, cortex.create_dataset_version and cortex.propose_training_job; training (behaviour cloning with ACT or SmolVLA) starts after a person approves the GPU job in the studio.
- Can Claude Code train a robot? Yes, in simulation. Run claude mcp add --transport http cortex http://localhost:3000/mcp and ask Claude Code to teach the arm a task; it calls cortex.* tools and reads the results. It never sends motor commands: Cortex validates every target and executes it with inverse kinematics, and the simulator decides whether an attempt succeeded.
- How do I collect demonstrations for an SO-101 with LeRobot in MuJoCo? cortex.start_agent_collection runs autonomous attempts in fresh simulator seeds, planned by a vision-language model or by the scripted IK oracle (labelled as such); only simulator-verified successes are saved, as LeRobotDataset v3 episodes. Your agent can also drive the arm itself with cortex.robot_start_episode and the cortex.robot_* tools, or import existing recordings from the Hugging Face Hub with cortex.import_demonstrations.
- How do I evaluate a robot policy in simulation? cortex.evaluate_learned_policy runs a trained checkpoint in three seeded MuJoCo branches (baseline, shifted object, dim lighting) on held-out seeds. Success rates are reported with 95% Wilson confidence intervals, and cortex.compare_experiments gives branch-by-branch deltas and p-values between runs.
- How do I improve an ACT policy with targeted demonstrations or RL? cortex.improve_policy finds the weakest measured condition of the latest evaluation, collects new demonstrations there in fresh seeds, builds a new dataset version and proposes retraining. For reinforcement learning, cortex.get_policy_weaknesses lists the measured weak conditions and cortex.propose_rl_sandboxes proposes RL sandboxes for them, each with an estimated uplift and cost (a labelled estimate, not a measurement); you accept them with cortex.accept_rl_sandboxes. Successful RL rollouts become demonstrations that retrain ACT.
- Is there an MCP server for robotics? Cortex is one: a Model Context Protocol server over streamable HTTP at http://localhost:3000/mcp, exposing intake, simulation, data collection, dataset, training, evaluation and improvement tools as cortex.*. The same tools answer on REST at http://localhost:8000/api/tools, and calls are attributed to the agent in the audit log.
- Can the agent train and deploy on the physical robot arm? That is where the loop leads: after simulation, the policy moves to the physical SO-101 to keep training on real demonstrations and then run the task on the line. Today the whole loop runs in MuJoCo, and a real arm runs a policy only through a local bridge with an operator present, joint, velocity and workspace limits, a watchdog and an e-stop; the API and MCP cannot drive the hardware directly.

- [Full tool reference](http://localhost:5173/llms-full.txt): all 57 registry tools with descriptions, arguments and JSON schemas
- [MCP discovery document](http://localhost:5173/.well-known/mcp.json): endpoint, transport, REST mirror and tool list
- [MCP Server Card](http://localhost:5173/server-card.json): SEP-2127 server card
- [MCP server README](https://github.com/psamin/speculativespeculativeagentaction/blob/main/mcp/README.md): tool table, approvals, long-running jobs
- [Studio](http://localhost:5173/studio): the web app where people review data and approve training
